name: Sun Yat-sen
role: Chinese revolutionary; first provisional president of the Republic of China (1912); founder of the Kuomintang
summary: Sun Yat-sen led the revolution that ended the Qing monarchy and built his politics on the Three Principles of nationalism, popular sovereignty and the people's livelihood. He proposed a republic reached through military rule and party tutelage, with a five-Yuan government, examinations and local self-government, and state-led industrial development financed by foreign capital. He rejected Marxian class struggle while cooperating with Soviet Russia.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: His republic abolished the imperial throne, and his democracy rests on popular election and examination for office rather than birth.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: His revolutionary career consisted of small conspiratorial leagues and armed risings aiming to start the revolution.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: He wanted China to adopt machinery and "make capitalism create socialism" so that the two forces work side by side, treating capitalist development as a base for a better society.

civilizational-union.rationale: He urged Asian peoples, with Russia as an ally, to join in a common cause based on the Oriental rule of Right.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: He condemned the West's domination of Asian peoples as the rule of Might and sought their emancipation.

class-collaboration.rationale: He proposed his development scheme partly so that the class struggle between capital and labour could be avoided, and regarded the class struggle as a social disease.

class-struggle-history.rationale: He rejected class struggle as the driver of history, calling Marx a pathologist who knew the diseases of social evolution but not its principle.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: He denounced Europe treating India, Persia, Arabia and others as colonies and called for ending their oppression.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Popular sovereignty is the second principle of his programme, with final power returned to a People's Congress after the tutelage period.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Articles 22-23 have the draft constitution promulgated by a People's Congress of delegates from self-governing counties, not by the government alone.

decide-locally.rationale: Article 17 sets central and provincial authority in equilibrium with no tendency to centralisation or decentralisation, while making the county the unit of self-government.

defeat-communism.rationale: He allied his party with Soviet Russia and sought cooperation with the Chinese Communists, rather than seeking to defeat them.

delink-world-market.rationale: He aimed to make China an "Economic Ocean" absorbing the surplus capital and goods of the industrial nations, integrating it with the world economy.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: He objected to a permanent class dictatorship, preferring a provisional party tutelage leading to democracy, and doubted Russia's "absolute popular government."

direct-votes.rationale: In the constitutional period the People's Congress exercises initiative and referendum over central laws and citizens of self-governed counties hold the four powers, though representative bodies remain.

dominated-front.rationale: In the Pan-Asianism speech he asked the oppressed peoples of Asia to unite against the Western rule of Might and called Pan-Asianism the cause of the oppressed.

duties-before-rights.rationale: He held that Chinese had too much liberty and should sacrifice individual liberty for the organised nation.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: His programme opened China to foreign capital and trade to end commercial struggle, the opposite of a closed self-sufficient bloc.

elective-rulers.rationale: He founded a republic in which officials are elected and recalled by the people, and condemned any ruler's ambition for the throne.

ethnic-nation.rationale: He framed one Chinese race-nation yet adopted a five-race republic and promised weak racial groups self-determination, so his sources point both ways.

every-country-ready-for-democracy.rationale: His plan makes a period of political tutelage compulsory so the government can train the people in political ability before they exercise the four powers.

experts-over-public.rationale: He divided men into natural classes, with experts administering (neng) while the people hold political power (ch'uan), so policy-making stays with the majority but administration with experts.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: He split industry between private enterprise, left alone where it does the job better, and national undertakings, so his record on markets versus state points both ways.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: He explained history through the Confucian idea of benevolence (jen), which Linebarger notes contradicts the Marxian materialist interpretation of history.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: He spent his career in the anti-monarchical movement, led the revolution that ended the Manchu throne, and served as first provisional president of the Republic.

national-resource-control.rationale: He wanted China's mines and natural resources developed as state-owned undertakings, with foreign capital and managers only until loans were repaid.

national-self-determination.rationale: He called for the emancipation of oppressed Asian peoples from the rule of Might and for helping weak racial groups toward self-determination, while claiming China's existing territory as one nation.

natural-rulers.rationale: His scheme kept a doctrine of intellectual inequality among natural classes of men, with a leader class preserved by examination.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: His min sheng principle was meant to avoid the evils of capitalism without the Marxian class-war programme.

office-by-exam.rationale: Article 15 requires every candidate and appointed official, central or local, to pass the Central Government's examinations or be certified by its personnel registry.

one-party-rule.rationale: He made the Kuomintang, reorganised on the Communist pattern, the designated leader of the people through the tutelage period.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: The Kuomintang he reorganised had strong central control that assured orthodoxy, with dissent expressed only by schism.

patriotic-education.rationale: Article 6 has the government spread its doctrines to enlighten the people and promote national unity.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: His ideology rebuilt Chinese nationalism on old Chinese morality and knowledge joined with Western science.

property-fundamental.rationale: His land plan lets the local government buy land at the owner's declared value at any time and keeps unearned increment for the people.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: He kept private landownership but gave rises in land value from social progress to the public, saying owners should not keep them as private benefit.

public-ownership.rationale: His development plan makes railways, harbours, mines and other major undertakings state owned and managed for the benefit of the whole nation.

recall-officials.rationale: Articles 9 and 24 give citizens of self-governed counties and the People's Congress the power of recall over local and central officials.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Linebarger records that Sun favoured the regulation of capital at all points and public ownership in some.

sacred-ruler.rationale: His republican revolution rejected the Manchu emperor, and he condemned Caesarism and ambitions for the throne unequivocally.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: He built his whole programme on inviting foreign capital, foreign experts and organisers to develop China.

separated-powers.rationale: He designed a five-Yuan government (executive, legislative, judicial, examination, control) that divides authority among separate bodies, though before a constitution the Yuan heads answer to the President.

state-directs-investment.rationale: He proposed a state development programme of national undertakings in transport, iron and steel, mining and water power, financed with foreign capital under state ownership.

territorial-expansion.rationale: He rejected the rule of Might and aggression against weaker peoples, calling instead for a civilization of peace and equality.

traditional-family.rationale: He treated the family and clan as the base on which loyalty to the nation should be built, and planned to organise clans nationally.

workers-councils.rationale: He chose liberal government through ch'uan and neng in place of a dictatorship of the proletariat operating through soviets.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: He described foreign economic pressure on China as an "immense tribute" that had reduced it to a sub-colony.

notes: Sources: the Fundamentals of National Reconstruction, The International Development of China, the Pan-Asianism speech, and Linebarger's exposition quoting the San Min Chu I lectures. The lectures themselves were not available in full text. Themes searched: government, economy, world, society, liberty, means, culture; religion, gender, drugs, technology and ecology have no recorded position.
